questions.answer: Not in the warehouse. It holds no wind generation figure for ERCOT on 6 November 2026. Neither ERCOT's daily wind and solar table (ercot_wind_solar_hsl_daily) nor the hourly EIA-930 net generation table (eia930_all_generation) has any rows for that day. Both tables have rows for dates before and after it, so the day itself is missing. I can't give a figure without estimating one.

questions.question: What was the highest hourly demand in ERCOT in the week of Monday 2 to Sunday 8 November 2026 (Central time), in MW?
questions.answer: The week is only partly held, so I can't give its true peak. The table has 72 of the 168 hours for Monday 2 to Sunday 8 November 2026 (Central time). The held hours are 2 to 4 November, plus the Central-time hours from 12 am Thursday 5 November onward that fall before 6 pm UTC... no: the missing run is 5 to 8 November UTC. Among the held hours, the highest ERCOT hourly demand was 65,888 MW, at 3 pm Central on 2 November 2026 (eia930_all_demand, EIA-930, series eia930:ERCO). The hours from about 6 pm Central on 4 November to 6 pm Central on 8 November are missing. Demand in those hours could be higher, so 65,888 MW is the maximum of the held hours only.

questions.question: What was the average hourly day-ahead price at ERCOT's hub average (HB_HUBAVG) in the week of Monday 2 to Sunday 8 November 2026 (Central time), in USD per MWh?
questions.answer: The full week of Monday 2 to Sunday 8 November 2026 (Central time) is not held, so I can't give a figure for it. The day-ahead table (iso_dam_hub_prices) holds only 120 of the week's 168 hours. Those hours run from 12 am Central on 2 November to 11 pm Central on 6 November. Saturday 7 and Sunday 8 November are missing. Over those 120 hours, the mean hourly day-ahead price at ERCOT HB_HUBAVG (spp_dam) was 39.24 USD/MWh (iso_dam_hub_prices). That is the mean of the hours held, not of the whole week.

questions.question: What was the average hourly nuclear generation in the Lower 48 states in the week of Monday 2 to Sunday 8 November 2026 (UTC), in MW?
questions.answer: The warehouse holds only part of that week, so I can't give a figure for the whole week. It has hours for 2 to 4 November 2026 (UTC), which is 72 of the week's 168 hours. For those 72 hours, mean Lower 48 nuclear net generation was 79,920.44 MW (eia930_all_generation, EIA-930, source tier). It holds no hours for 5 to 8 November 2026 (UTC), so that 79,920.44 MW is not the Monday-to-Sunday average.
